# Talk scaffold — build the single deck talk.pdf from 00_00.tex with lualatex
# (fontspec + minted). Run inside the nix shell, see README.md:
#   nix-shell -p gnumake 'python3.pkgs.pygments' \
#     '(texlive.combine { inherit (texlive) scheme-medium substr collection-latexextra; })' \
#     --run "make"
LATEX  ?= lualatex
FLAGS  ?= -shell-escape -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error
MAIN   := 00_00.tex
OUT    := talk
THEME  := theme/beamerthememosaic.sty
SECTNS := $(wildcard sections/*.tex)

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(OUT).pdf

# -jobname=talk keeps artefacts as talk.* while the source stays 00_00.tex.
# Two passes: first for aux/toc, second to settle toc + nav.
$(OUT).pdf: $(MAIN) $(THEME) $(SECTNS) $(wildcard images/icons/*.pdf)
	$(LATEX) $(FLAGS) -jobname=$(OUT) $(MAIN)
	-$(LATEX) $(FLAGS) -jobname=$(OUT) $(MAIN)

clean:
	rm -f $(OUT).pdf $(OUT).aux $(OUT).log $(OUT).nav $(OUT).out $(OUT).snm $(OUT).toc $(OUT).vrb
	rm -rf _minted-*
# mosaic-talk — "How AI Writes"

A self-contained, one-off session deck: **how a generative AI writes** —
tokens → embeddings → attention → next-word election → the loop — pitched at
AI newcomers (teen audience): plain language, playful analogies, no jargon
walls. Beamer `mosaic` theme (ported from the 451 course theme) plus a
curated slice of the Streamline Mosaic icon set.

The title slide states the session intent; every frame carries
`% PRESENTER:` comments with speaker guidance (pacing, live demos, questions
to ask the room). TODOs mark the few personalisation spots (contact, links,
date).

## Build

dawn has no system texlive — build inside the nix shell (lualatex for
fontspec, `-shell-escape` for minted/Pygments):

```bash
nix-shell -p gnumake 'python3.pkgs.pygments' \
  '(texlive.combine { inherit (texlive) scheme-medium substr collection-latexextra; })' \
  --run "make"
```

`make` runs two lualatex passes over `00_00.tex` (jobname `talk`) so the
toc/nav settle, producing **`talk.pdf`** (~52 pages — overlays expand the
frames into reveal steps). First run pulls the texlive closure (~6 min);
after that it's fast. `make clean` removes artefacts.

On a machine with a full texlive + Pygments, plain `make` also works.
Note: `\date` is a hardcoded placeholder — `\today` renders as a 1980
epoch date inside the nix reproducible-build shell.

## Where things live

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `00_00.tex` | Main deck: metadata + `\input`s the sections |
| `sections/motivation.tex` | The hook + the big secret ("very well-read autocomplete") |
| `sections/tokens.tex` | Step 1 — tokens as LEGO bricks (reveal diagram) |
| `sections/embeddings.tex` | Step 2 — map of meaning (tinted-halo scatter) |
| `sections/attention.tex` | Step 3 — attention arrows, thickness = who matters |
| `sections/cache.tex` | The note stack — KV cache as accumulating sticky notes |
| `sections/mlp.tex` | Inside the think box — sparse MLP neuron wall |
| `sections/predict.tex` | Step 4 — next-word election bars + the loop diagram |
| `sections/architecture.tex` | The whole cake — layer stack, Steps 1–4 tagged |
| `sections/training.tex` | How it learned (read / guess / check / repeat) |
| `sections/takeaways.tex`, `sections/closing.tex` | Wrap-up + Q&A |
| `theme/` | Vendored beamer theme (`mosaic`). Fix upstream and re-vendor, don't edit ad hoc |
| `theme/static/logo.png` | Title-page logo — swap for your own white/transparent PNG |
| `images/icons/` | Icon PDFs (+ `svg/` sources); see `ICONS.md` |
| `ICONS.md` | Icon registry: what each icon is for, how to add one |

## Presentation notes

- Overlays: every diagram reveals step by step (`\visible`, one reveal per
  click); bullets pause too. Present straight through — the deck is animated
  as built.
- All diagrams are inline TikZ (no external images); edit coordinates in the
  section files if you want to change the examples.
- The attention slide (star of the deck) has a swap trick in its presenter
  comment: change "it was shiny" to "it was guarding" to flip which word
  matters.
- The note-stack slide is the KV cache without the acronym; the MLP slide's
  sparsity beat echoes the ~27k-neuron layers studied with SAEs (see the
  presenter comment there).

## Icons — license note

Icons are from the **Streamline Mosaic** set (streamlinehq.com). The license
allows up to **50 icons per project**; this repo is its own project and uses
**9 / 50**. Adding icons: pick from the library in the 451 builder repo
(`451_builder/*/*.svg`), follow `ICONS.md` §Adding an icon. Don't exceed the
cap, and don't share icons between projects against their counts.

# Beamer RL: Slide Construction Platform & TikZ Studio

A comprehensive platform and field guide for creating, evaluating, and optimizing modern 16:9 educational slide decks in LaTeX Beamer on top of the **QMUL theme**.

Features an **RL Pairwise Slide Rating Platform** (for preference optimization / DPO / RLHF), a **TikZ Diagram Studio** tuned for widescreen slide geometry, starter templates, and an automated visual overflow auditing pipeline.

---

## Key Features

1. 🏛️ **Built on the QMUL Template**:
   - Uses the official QMUL presentation theme ([`theme/`](file:///home/dawn/d/beamer_rl/theme/)) and iconography set ([`icons/`](file:///home/dawn/d/beamer_rl/icons/)).
   - Clean 16:9 widescreen layout (`aspectratio=169`), `qmblue` palette, rounded shadowed blocks, and footline frame numbers.
2. ⚖️ **RL Pairwise Slide Rating Platform**:
   - Side-by-side visual comparison of competing slide constructions (**Slide A** vs **Slide B**).
   - Preference rating slider from **0 to 10** (0 = Strongly prefer Left, 5 = Neutral, 10 = Strongly prefer Right).
   - Quality factor tagging: margin overflows, code readability, clutter, "show-then-do" cadence, TikZ clarity.
   - Saves ratings directly to [`data/preference_dataset.jsonl`](file:///home/dawn/d/beamer_rl/data/preference_dataset.jsonl) in standard DPO / reward modeling format (`chosen`, `rejected`, `score`, `critique`).
   - Includes a benchmark gallery of real slide dilemmas ([`data/benchmark_pairs.json`](file:///home/dawn/d/beamer_rl/data/benchmark_pairs.json)) plus a live sandbox for testing arbitrary TeX snippets.
3. 📐 **TikZ Diagram Studio**:
   - Designed specifically for constructing and validating diagrams on the 16:9 Beamer canvas.
   - **Preamble Hoisting Enforcer**: Isolates `\tikzset{...}` styles from the diagram body, eliminating TeX parameter (`#1`) compiler crashes.
   - **Canvas Safe Boundary**: Guides diagrams to fit cleanly within the $14\,\text{cm} \times 6.5\,\text{cm}$ slide safe zone.
   - **Certified Template Library**: Memory pointer models, data pipelines, collision-free binary trees/ASTs, layered architecture stacks, and state transition machines.
4. 🖼️ **Icon Usage & Layout Studio (Stream 3)**:
   - **Instructor Design Ruling**: Enforces full-height visual anchors ($\ge 4.5\text{cm}$) over deprecated tiny ($0.45\text{cm}$) heading marks.
   - **37-Asset Course Catalog**: Categorized by domain (Development, Interface, Business, Education, Design, Technology, Social).
   - **Widescreen Layout Archetypes**: Split 50/50 hero anchors, milestone section cards, 'Your Turn' task blocks, 4-pillar data pipelines, and error triage boards.
   - **Live LuaLaTeX Compiler & DPO Gallery**: Test icon positioning tradeoffs in real-time and export production-ready Beamer LaTeX code.
5. 📄 **Canonical Demonstration Deck**:
   - [`guide_deck.tex`](file:///home/dawn/d/beamer_rl/guide_deck.tex) (compiled to [`.build/guide_deck.pdf`](file:///home/dawn/d/beamer_rl/.build/guide_deck.pdf)): 29 slides teaching Beamer construction rules *using Beamer itself*.
6. 📋 **Dual-Strand Templates**:
   - [`templates/lecture_template.tex`](file:///home/dawn/d/beamer_rl/templates/lecture_template.tex): Conceptual exposition, learning objectives with compliance codes, and divider cards.
   - [`templates/lab_template.tex`](file:///home/dawn/d/beamer_rl/templates/lab_template.tex): Interactive "show-then-do" cadence, `yourturn` task blocks, checkpoints, and plenary error triage.
7. 🔍 **Automated Visual QA Scanner**:
   - [`scripts/slide-margin-scan.py`](file:///home/dawn/d/beamer_rl/scripts/slide-margin-scan.py): Python tool rendering PDF pages via `pdftoppm` and computing ink bounding boxes to catch silent edge overflows.

---

## Quickstart & Launch

### 1. Launch the Interactive RL Platform & TikZ Studio
```bash
# Launch via Make:
make app

# Or directly with Streamlit:
streamlit run app.py
```
Visit `http://localhost:8501` to compare slide pairs, rate them on the 0-10 slider, and build TikZ diagrams.

### 2. Compile Decks & Run Automated Margin QA
```bash
# Build the demonstration deck and all starter templates
make all

# Build only the canonical guide deck (.build/guide_deck.pdf)
make guide

# Build only the templates (.build/templates/*.pdf)
make templates

# Run the automated ink-boundary overflow QA scan
make scan

# Clean intermediate files (.build/, *.vrb, _minted*)
make clean
```

### 3. Reproducible Nix Environment
```bash
# Drop into the pinned TeX Live 2024 + Pygments + Streamlit + Poppler shell
nix-shell --run 'make all'
nix-shell --run 'make app'
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
slide-margin-scan.py — Automated Ink-Bounding Box & Margin Outlier Scanner

Renders every page of a PDF to PNG at specified DPI, detects ink bounding boxes,
determines normal margin envelopes, and flags outlier pages with content spills.
"""

import sys
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import json
import statistics
from PIL import Image

def ink_bbox(image_path):
    im = Image.open(image_path).convert("L")
    w, h = im.size
    # Sample four corners to detect slide background color
    corners = [
        im.getpixel((2, 2)),
        im.getpixel((w - 3, 2)),
        im.getpixel((2, h - 3)),
        im.getpixel((w - 3, h - 3))
    ]
    bg = max(set(corners), key=corners.count)
    # Binary mask: any pixel significantly different from background is considered "ink"
    bw = im.point(lambda v: 255 if abs(v - bg) > 25 else 0)
    bbox = bw.getbbox()
    return (w, h, bbox)

def scan_pdf(pdf_path, dpi=60, workdir="/tmp/slidescan_guide"):
    base = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(pdf_path))[0]
    outdir = os.path.join(workdir, base)
    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Clean previous page renderings
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(outdir, "*.png")):
        os.remove(f)

    # Render pages using pdftoppm
    pdftoppm_bin = "pdftoppm"
    # Fallback to local nix store if pdftoppm not in standard PATH
    if not subprocess.run(["which", "pdftoppm"], capture_output=True).returncode == 0:
        poppler_paths = glob.glob("/nix/store/*poppler*/bin/pdftoppm")
        if poppler_paths:
            pdftoppm_bin = poppler_paths[0]

    cmd = [pdftoppm_bin, "-png", "-r", str(dpi), pdf_path, os.path.join(outdir, "p")]
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

    pages = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(outdir, "p*.png")))
    if not pages:
        return [], 0, (0, 0, 0, 0)

    boxes = []
    for p in pages:
        w, h, b = ink_bbox(p)
        boxes.append((p, w, h, b))

content.text:
I've reworked all 8 diagrams, committed them to `opus-visuals` (e4e8dac) and pushed. Nothing is merged to main, so Alex can review the diff. The deck is now **67 pages**, down from 69. The README said ~52, which was out of date; it now says 67.

**Why the visuals weren't landing:** most of them stated the idea in a caption and the drawing didn't show it. Four problems kept coming up:
- **The "before" vanished when the "after" appeared.** On the tokens slide, the sentence disappeared on the first click.
- **The picture contradicted its own analogy.** The map's axes put a cat as "less alive" than a king, and the KV cache explainer still printed the "K V" acronym.
- **Arrows meaning different things overlapped,** or pointed at the wrong place.
- **Some text and lines were too small or faint for a projector.**

| Diagram | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Tokens** | Plain boxes, nothing like LEGO. Click 2 erased the sentence, so you never saw the "chop". "Longer words get split" was only a bullet. | The sentence stays up while scissors snip it, and bricks with LEGO studs drop out underneath. Then the ID numbers appear ("the model sees: 464 9379 …"), and "skateboarding" splits into skate/board/ing. 8 → 6 pages. |
| **Map of meaning** | Made-up axes the points contradicted. Banana sat alone, so "close = similar" had only one contrast. | No axis labels, just a faint map grid with three tinted neighbourhoods: pets, royalty, food. A "puppy?" click lets the room guess before it lands next to dog. |
| **Attention** | Several arrows started from one spot above "it", so they bunched up. Thin lines at 35% grey would vanish on a projector. Didn't show "every word looks at every word". | Asks "what does it mean?" first. Then "it" looks at every word with equal arcs that nest and never cross. Then they re-weight: gold thick, shiny as the clue, dragon a second look. Faint lines darkened. 7 → 6 pages. |
| **Note stack** | Showed the "K V" acronym the notes say to avoid. The read and write arrows sat almost on top of each other, and both looked like they pointed at the new note. Double orange outlines. | Sticky-note drawings instead of "K V". Reading is an orange sweep left across the stack; writing is a red arrow straight down into an empty slot. Captions 1 and 2 match those colours. |
| **MLP** | Readable, but "gathered meaning → thought it over" was vague. | The input box carries the attention answer ("it = the shiny gold"). The output adds "+ gold is treasure, + dragons hoard it", so you can see it recalling facts. |
| **Election** | Five colours that meant nothing, small labels, and the creativity line was told, not shown. | Favourite in green, the rest in blue. On the last click pizza turns orange with "…but sometimes!". Labels bigger. |
| **Loop** | An abstract "your text" box with a huge empty loop. Click 1 had an arrow pointing at nothing. | The box holds the real sentence. "mat" rides the red arrow back and the box becomes "…on the **mat**". Each arrow now appears with its target. 6 → 7 pages. |
| **Layer cake** | The example didn't match: "The dragon kept the gold" with an election over mat/sofa/roof. The loop arrow pointed into "gold", as if overwriting it. Step tags were tiny and used dotted lines. Layers were uneven widths. | One sentence end to end ("safe 40% \| hidden 25% \| forever 12%"). "safe" is added as a new brick after gold. A grey spine on the left shows the stack reads upward, and the Step 1–4 tags sit on it. All layers share one width. |
